lessons.summary: INSA Lyon offers a student-built robotics route through Clubelek, where mechanical parts, electronics, and software become competition robots.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

INSA Lyon offers a student-built robotics route through Clubelek, where mechanical parts, electronics, and software become competition robots.

![Clubelek main robot with smaller red robots in front](/img/lessons/orgs_school_2-insa-lyon.webp)
*Clubelek’s 2026 robots; photograph carries the Vercors Sciences mark. Source: [Official site](https://clubelek.fr/poles/coupe-de-france-de-robotique), Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Clubelek builds complete machines:** its competition group designs mechanisms, custom circuit boards, obstacle-avoiding routes, and image-recognition software.
- **Autonomous means self-directed:** robots execute the match without a human steering them, turning the competition rules into physical actions.
- **Picture the workspace:** the club describes a 2-by-3-metre field, or 6 square metres, with matches lasting 100 seconds.

> **Key idea:** A competition robot is an integration test of mechanics, electronics, and code, not just a clever strategy.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of API boundaries:** the strategy requests movement, but motors and mechanisms must actually deliver it; use this analogy to divide your team’s responsibilities.
- **Clubelek (INSA Lyon)** and **Coupe de France de Robotique** are related map nodes for exploring the student-team and event separately.
- **Learn from debugging:** the club’s 2024 interview describes electrical reliability problems and redesigning the rolling base, not merely adding more sophisticated algorithms.

## How to engage

1. **Watch a complete match** and list which actions require movement, sensing, or object handling; distinguish what you observe from what you infer.
2. **Read the club’s public introduction:** it explicitly welcomes visitors outside INSA, but arrange any visit through its published contact route.
3. **Propose one focused exchange:** bring a small demonstration and ask about testing or documentation rather than assuming access to equipment.

lessons.name: INSA Rennes
lessons.summary: INSA Rennes has a student robotics club that brings programming, electronics, and mechanics together to build autonomous competition robots.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

INSA Rennes has a student robotics club that brings programming, electronics, and mechanics together to build autonomous competition robots.

![Tall blue INSA Rennes robot with white mechanisms and blue wiring](/img/lessons/orgs_school_2-insa-rennes.webp)
*The club’s robot photographed for its 2026 competition report. Source: [Official site](https://www.club-robot.bzh/blog/coupe-2026), Tous droits réservés.*

## What they do in robotics

- **The Club Robot belongs to AEIR:** the school’s student association provides the organizational home for its robotics activity.
- **Mixed disciplines build one machine:** the club describes students combining computing, electronics, and mechanics, with beginners learning alongside experienced members.
- **Matches run autonomously:** the club describes 100-second rounds; that is 1 minute 40 seconds for the robot to execute its plan.

> **Key idea:** A short autonomous match exposes whether an entire student-built system works together.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Use an integration-test analogy:** a successful movement function is not enough; the complete robot must finish useful actions under match conditions.
- **Study a concrete codebase:** the club publishes a team2025 repository alongside its competition reports, offering software students an entry into a physical project.
- **Compare with INSA Lyon:** both offer student competition examples; use the Coupe de France de Robotique map node to understand their shared setting.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the linked first-series match:** the club’s 2026 report points to its appearance around 1:48:53 in the organizer’s recording.
2. **Browse team2025** and sketch the repository layout before attempting changes; treat season-specific code as an example, not a universal starter kit.
3. **Use the club’s published contact:** propose a technical discussion about one observed behavior or a small reproducible software contribution.

lessons.name: INSA Strasbourg
lessons.summary: INSA Strasbourg connects robotics teaching with mechatronics projects and a student competition club called CRIS.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

INSA Strasbourg connects robotics teaching with mechatronics projects and a student competition club called CRIS.

![Official INSA Strasbourg logo in red and grey](/img/lessons/orgs_school_2-insa-strasbourg.webp)
*Official INSA Strasbourg school logo. Source: [Official site](https://www.insa-strasbourg.fr/fr/mecatronique/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Mechatronics combines disciplines:** mechanical design, electronics, computing, and automatic control are taught together rather than as isolated components.
- **Students build working prototypes:** the school describes simple mobile robots from the second year, then more complex group projects.
- **CRIS adds competition practice:** its public site describes building robots for the French robotics championship; its featured season is 2023.

> **Key idea:** Robot design works best when the software interface and the physical mechanism are developed together.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of a full-stack application:** a camera, image-processing code, motion commands, and mechanism must agree, just as frontend and backend must share a contract.
- **A concrete 2026 example:** students built a LEGO EV3 portrait robot that turns camera images into contours, then draws them on A4 paper.
- **Follow CRIS – Club de Robotique de l'INSA de Strasbourg:** the map labels it separately from the school; ICube offers another related research direction.

## How to engage

1. **Start with the mechatronics program:** identify which parts of a small robot you understand and which require mechanical or electronics learning.
2. **Watch the CRIS electronics tutorial** to see how a printed circuit board, the physical board connecting components, enters the workflow.
3. **Use public club channels** for a focused question; confirm present activity before proposing a visit, since the club homepage describes an older season.

lessons.name: INSA Toulouse
lessons.summary: INSA Toulouse’s Club Robot teaches students to combine code, electronics, and mechanics while building robots for competition.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

INSA Toulouse’s Club Robot teaches students to combine code, electronics, and mechanics while building robots for competition.

![Two INSA Toulouse students stand behind their robot on a competition table](/img/lessons/orgs_school_2-insa-toulouse.webp)
*Club Robot INSA Toulouse at the 2024 Coupe de France. Source: [Official site](https://clubrobotinsat.github.io/competition/recap-cdf-2024), All rights reserved.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Club Robot INSA Toulouse builds a complete robot:** the club organizes around software, electronics, and mechanics rather than treating robotics as programming alone.
- **Training comes before specialization:** its introduction describes a first semester for teaching newcomers, followed by designing the season’s competition robot.
- **Public documentation covers development tools:** its online book explains software and electronics setup, while its blog records competition experience.

> **Key idea:** A student robotics club needs a reproducible learning and setup process as much as a working robot.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Treat onboarding like a development environment:** every teammate needs working tools before shared code can become a dependable physical demonstration.
- **Use a concrete reading exercise:** compare the 2019 training video with the 2024 report; distinguish a practice demonstration from evidence of competition performance.
- **Inspect the documentation’s scope:** it explicitly explains tool installation rather than documenting all robot code, so do not mistake it for a complete architecture guide.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the practice robot** and write down the sequence of visible actions, without assuming which sensors or algorithms caused them.
2. **Read the setup-book introduction** and note its contribution instructions; suggest a precise correction if a documented setup step is unclear.
3. **Contact the club through its public page:** propose a documentation exchange with 42AI and confirm arrangements instead of assuming membership or workshop access.

lessons.name: ISAE-ENSMA
lessons.summary: ISAE-ENSMA has a student robotics association, ENSMASTEEL, that designs autonomous robots and publishes competition projects.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

ISAE-ENSMA has a student robotics association, ENSMASTEEL, that designs autonomous robots and publishes competition projects.

![ENSMASTEEL students work on a robot beside a laptop at the competition](/img/lessons/orgs_school_2-isae-ensma.webp)
*ENSMASTEEL preparing a robot at the 2024 event. Source: [Official site](https://www.ensma.fr/des-eleves-ingenieurs-de-lisae-ensma-a-la-coupe-de-france-de-robotique/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **ENSMASTEEL builds autonomous machines:** the school’s 2024 report describes two teams and two robots, including a holonomic design.
- **Holonomic describes movement freedom:** the ezBot project concerns a robot intended for omnidirectional movement rather than only forward driving and turning.
- **The 2024 task involved plants:** robots moved and repotted them on a 2-by-3-metre game table, making object handling part of navigation.

> **Key idea:** Student robotics becomes easier to understand when you inspect the mechanical, electronic, and software artifacts together.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Read ezBot like a multi-service repository:** branches separate resources, electronics, mechanical models, and ROS 2, software for connecting robot programs.
- **A concrete comparison:** the 2024 school report contrasts a traditional robot with a holonomic one; ask what each design changes for motion planning.
- **Ensma Space Project (Ensmasteel)** is the related map entry for student activity; **Coupe de France de Robotique** explains the shared competition context.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the linked match recording:** the school points to about 1:19:06 for its 2024 robots; compare visible actions with the written report.
2. **Browse ezBot’s branches** and identify what belongs to electronics, mechanical design, or code before choosing one narrow area to explore.
3. **Use the public repository** for a reproducible technical question; check the relevant season and license before reusing any files.

lessons.name: ISAE-SUPAERO
lessons.summary: ISAE-SUPAERO combines student competition robotics with public robotics teaching and research demonstrations.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

ISAE-SUPAERO combines student competition robotics with public robotics teaching and research demonstrations.

![ISAE-SUPAERO robots on a game table with students cheering behind them](/img/lessons/orgs_school_2-isae-supaero.webp)
*Robotik club robots and students, published by the student association. Source: [Official site](https://www.ae-isae-supaero.fr/clubs/clubs-ae#Robotik), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Robotik builds robots from scratch:** the student association describes four groups covering low-level software, high-level software, mechanics, and electronics.
- **Low-level code drives hardware:** it controls actuators, the devices that create movement; high-level code decides the robot’s match strategy.
- **Teaching materials are public:** the Supaero robotics class publishes Python notebooks based on Pinocchio, a library for calculating robot geometry, motion, and forces.

> **Key idea:** The same institution can offer both hands-on robot integration and mathematical tools for understanding motion.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of layered APIs:** strategy calls movement operations while lower layers translate them into hardware commands; Robotik’s four groups make those boundaries concrete.
- **A worked research example:** the navigation team demonstrates combining laser distances, motion measurements, and satellite positioning to reconstruct part of the campus in 3D.
- **Connect to Pinocchio:** the map’s software node complements the school entry; INSA Toulouse provides a nearby student-club comparison, not an assumed formal partnership.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the campus reconstruction** and separate the visible reconstructed scene from assumptions about how accurate or complete it is.
2. **Open the public course repository:** start with an introductory notebook before trying the multi-target arm-control exercise.
3. **Use Robotik’s public channels** to propose one technical exchange about a small demo; do not assume the school’s laboratories accept external teams.

lessons.name: Isep
lessons.summary: Isep uses robotics in student projects, including educational robots and a documented Nao hackathon on education and inclusion.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Isep uses robotics in student projects, including educational robots and a documented Nao hackathon on education and inclusion.

![Students work in groups with laptops during the Isep and La Salle-Saint Nicolas hackathon](/img/lessons/orgs_school_2-isep.webp)
*The January 2025 Nao hackathon brought Isep and school students together. Source: [Official site](https://www.isep.fr/cordees-reussite-isep-saint-nicolas-2025/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **The January 2025 hackathon used Nao:** Isep reports 60 participants, organized into 10 teams, working on education and health-related ideas.
- **One project made Nao a game master:** participants answered subject questions while following a story, connecting a physical robot with an interactive learning experience.
- **AIR is a historical competition route:** a 2020 interview describes the Association Isépienne de Robotique; its present activity is unknown from that source.

> **Key idea:** A robot can be an interface for a learning activity, not just a machine that moves objects.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of a conversational frontend:** the visible robot presents an interaction, while application code determines questions and responses; this analogy helps separate behavior from hardware.
- **A concrete scale comparison:** 60 participants across 10 teams averages 6 people per team, though the report does not specify equal-sized teams.
- **Explore NAO and HRI foundations & user-study methods:** the latter concerns studying human–robot interaction, rather than treating an engaging demo as proof of usefulness.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the local-news report** linked by Isep and identify which interactions are actually demonstrated versus described as project ambitions.
2. **Inspect ISEP-R0B0:** this historical LISITE project repository documents a web interface using Blockly, a tool for constructing programs from visual blocks.
3. **Ask through public school channels** about educational-robotics exchanges; distinguish a past event or repository from an open invitation to use equipment.

lessons.name: KAIST
lessons.summary: KAIST hosts multiple robotics groups, including the DRCD Lab, which combines custom legged hardware with learned movement controllers.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

KAIST hosts multiple robotics groups, including the DRCD Lab, which combines custom legged hardware with learned movement controllers.

![Blue and silver KAIST HOUND robot running on an athletics track](/img/lessons/orgs_school_2-kaist.webp)
*HOUND running on the track during the work reported in December 2023. Source: [Official site](https://news.kaist.ac.kr/newsen/html/news/?mng_no=60690&mode=V), All Rights Reserved.*

## What they do in robotics

- **DRCD builds HOUND:** KAIST HOUND 1 is a four-legged robot; its lab page describes a 45-kilogram machine designed for fast outdoor movement.
- **A controller produces commands:** HOUND’s 2023 sprint used reinforcement learning, learning behavior through reward-guided trials in simulation, a virtual world.
- **KAIST is broader than one robot:** RIRO Lab also publishes work on robot manipulation, planning, and interaction with people.

> **Key idea:** Fast learned movement depends on hardware design and realistic training, not a neural network in isolation.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of simulation as a test environment:** the training setup incorporated motor limits rather than assuming commands could produce unlimited motion.
- **Work through the sprint:** 100 metres divided by 19.87 seconds is about 5.03 metres per second on average, not the robot’s instantaneous peak speed.
- **Compare KAIST HOUND 1 and KAIST HOUND 2:** both are map nodes; the second platform’s page describes lab-designed motors, drivers, gears, and communication modules.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the lab’s sprint video** and separate what it proves about this run from claims about general outdoor autonomy.
2. **Read the HOUND platform pages** alongside the university’s dated announcement; do not mix specifications from different robot generations.
3. **Choose a specific lab publication** before contacting its public research channel; bring a reproducible question rather than requesting unspecified access to robots.

lessons.name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT)
lessons.summary: MIT develops robotics research and public teaching materials, including the Robot Locomotion Group’s work on manipulation, planning, and control.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

MIT develops robotics research and public teaching materials, including the Robot Locomotion Group’s work on manipulation, planning, and control.

![Two robot arms manipulate a white bucket on a table](/img/lessons/orgs_school_2-mit.webp)
*MIT contact-rich manipulation research. Image: Courtesy of the researchers. Source: [Official site](https://news.mit.edu/2023/ai-technique-robots-manipulate-objects-whole-bodies-0824), Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial No Derivatives license.*

## What they do in robotics

- **The Robot Locomotion Group belongs to CSAIL**, MIT’s Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory; its focus includes manipulation, meaning moving and handling objects.
- **Planning chooses a motion:** MIT’s 2023 example rotates a bucket by 180 degrees, or half a turn, while reasoning about physical contact.
- **Public materials connect theory to experiments:** lab tours show research projects, while Robotic Manipulation notes include interactive examples and exercises.

> **Key idea:** Models of physical contact can make robot planning more efficient than treating every interaction as a black box.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think beyond a pure function:** a grasp changes the physical world, so the next command depends on contact, geometry, and what the robot can observe.
- **Drake is a related map node:** its project page says it began in MIT’s group, but core development is now led by Toyota Research Institute.
- **Start with one accessible experiment:** the introductory manipulation chapter connects everyday tasks to simulation instead of requiring students to reproduce an entire research system.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the lab overview** to identify a project that fits your interests, then read its specific explanation before contacting anyone.
2. **Work through an introductory notebook** from the manipulation notes; record assumptions and failures rather than only a successful animation.
3. **Use public documentation and issue channels** for technical questions; share a minimal reproducible example and avoid assuming research hardware is available to external students.
